canon.title: Vienna, 1890–1938
canon.about: Classical facts of Vienna from the 1890s to the Anschluss, the integrated history par excellence, where music, art, letters, philosophy, science and politics meet in one city: from the schoolboy Hofmannsthal reading his verse to Schnitzler to Freud's departure for London in June 1938. A seed canon, drafted from general knowledge by a language model, each assertion naming the standard reference it is to be checked against; none is checked yet. Its selection bias, stated plainly: it follows the canonical intellectual history of Vienna 1900 (Schorske, Janik and Toulmin, Kandel), and so the famous, the male, the bourgeois and the written; the Vienna of workers, of Czech and other migrants, of most women, of popular culture and of Red Vienna's politics is almost absent, and the record's loops and shells gather round a few celebrated circles.

beings.name: The Vienna Court Opera (from 1918 the State Opera)
Society for Private Musical Performances (Verein für musikalische Privataufführungen)
The Vienna Secession (Vereinigung bildender Künstler Österreichs)

occasions.label: The schoolboy Hofmannsthal, writing as Loris, reads his verse to Schnitzler and the young writers of the Café Griensteidl
Schnitzler's Anatol in book form, with a verse prologue by Loris
Breuer and Freud, On the psychical mechanism of hysterical phenomena: preliminary communication
Klimt commissioned to paint Philosophy, Medicine and Jurisprudence for the ceiling of the University's great hall
occasions.note: The commission came through the Ministry of Education, shared with Franz Matsch.

occasions.label: Boltzmann returns to Vienna, to Stefan's chair of theoretical physics
Mach called to a chair of philosophy, for the history and theory of the inductive sciences
Breuer and Freud, Studies on Hysteria
Franz Joseph refuses to confirm Lueger, elected by the city council, as mayor
occasions.note: The emperor refused confirmation more than once (1895-1896) before yielding in 1897.

occasions.label: Altenberg's first book, Wie ich es sehe, published by S. Fischer on Kraus's recommendation
occasions.note: Kraus is said to have sent Altenberg's sketches to Fischer; to check.

occasions.label: Freud's estrangement from Breuer, recorded in his letters to Fliess
occasions.note: A gradual break (1894-1896), not a single meeting: an occasion of coarse resolution.

occasions.label: Kraus's satire Die demolirte Literatur on Young Vienna and the Café Griensteidl
The Vienna Secession founded, with Klimt its president
occasions.note: 3 April 1897 is the date usually given.

occasions.label: Franz Joseph confirms Lueger as mayor of Vienna
Mahler's debut at the Court Opera, conducting Lohengrin
Mahler made director of the Court Opera
occasions.note: 8 October 1897 is the date usually given.

occasions.label: The first number of Kraus's Die Fackel, against the press and above all the Neue Freie Presse
occasions.note: Kraus had declined an offer of a post at the Presse from its editor Moriz Benedikt.

occasions.label: Alma Schindler begins to study composition with Zemlinsky
occasions.note: The month is to be checked; the lessons ran into late 1901.

occasions.label: Boltzmann leaves his Vienna chair for Leipzig
occasions.note: Among his reasons, discomfort with Mach's influence in Vienna; he returned in 1902.

occasions.label: Mahler conducts the premiere of Zemlinsky's opera Es war einmal at the Court Opera
Klimt's Philosophy shown at the Secession; professors of the University petition against it
occasions.note: Some 87 professors signed the petition.

occasions.label: Mach, partly paralysed by a stroke in 1898, retires from the University
Meitner enters the University, among its first women students of physics
Schoenberg marries Mathilde Zemlinsky, his teacher's sister
Alma Schindler meets Mahler at Berta Zuckerkandl's dinner, Klimt among the guests
occasions.note: Klimt's presence rests on Alma's diaries and memoirs.

occasions.label: Alma breaks off her lessons and her attachment to Zemlinsky for Mahler
Meitner attends Boltzmann's lectures after his return to his chair
Freud given the title of extraordinary professor, by a decree the emperor signs
occasions.note: Long delayed; Gay tells of the patronage that finally won it.

occasions.label: Mahler marries Alma Schindler in the Karlskirche
The Secession's Beethoven exhibition round Klinger's statue: Klimt's Beethoven Frieze; Mahler conducts his arrangement for winds from the Ninth at the opening
occasions.note: The fourteenth exhibition, opened mid-April 1902. That the frieze's knight bears Mahler's features is often said and contested.

occasions.label: Zemlinsky and Schoenberg found the Vereinigung schaffender Tonkünstler, Mahler its honorary president
occasions.note: Founded in the spring of 1904; its concerts began that autumn.

occasions.label: Otto Wagner's church am Steinhof (1904-1907), with Moser's stained-glass windows, consecrated
occasions.note: Moser's design for the altar mosaic was rejected; the windows are his.

occasions.label: Berg and Webern begin their studies with Schoenberg
The Klimt group leaves the Secession
Meitner's doctorate in physics, her dissertation approved by Exner and Boltzmann
occasions.note: That Boltzmann was among the examiners is to be checked; Exner supervised the thesis.

occasions.label: Death of Boltzmann, by his own hand
Schiele admitted to the Academy of Fine Arts
The premieres of Schoenberg's First Quartet and Chamber Symphony; Mahler defends him against the hissing
The Academy of Fine Arts rejects Hitler after its drawing examination
Mahler's last performance as director of the Court Opera, Fidelio, after his resignation
Mahler and Alma leave for New York, seen off at the Westbahnhof by his admirers; Klimt: Vorbei
occasions.note: The date is firm; the list of those present follows Paul Stefan's account as de La Grange gives it, and is to be checked name by name.

occasions.label: The Kunstschau of the Klimt group: The Kiss shown, Kokoschka's first showing; Loos discovers Kokoschka
occasions.note: Loos's meeting with Kokoschka there is the usual account.

occasions.label: The Academy of Fine Arts does not admit Hitler even to its examination
Schiele leaves the Academy and founds the Neukunstgruppe
occasions.note: Spring 1909; the month is to be checked.

occasions.label: The International Kunstschau: Schiele exhibits at Klimt's invitation; Kokoschka's Murderer, Hope of Women staged
occasions.note: Kokoschka's play was staged in its garden theatre on 4 July 1909; the opening and closing dates are approximate.

occasions.label: Through Loos, Kokoschka paints Kraus, Altenberg and Loos himself
occasions.note: The portraits fall in 1909 and 1910; one occasion of coarse resolution.

occasions.label: Freud and Mahler walk for four hours through Leiden
occasions.note: 26 August 1910 is the day usually given. Mahler came in the crisis of Alma's affair with Gropius.

occasions.label: Mahler conducts the premiere of his Eighth Symphony, dedicated to Alma; Strauss in the audience
occasions.note: Strauss's presence is reported; to check.

occasions.label: Loos's house on the Michaelerplatz: building halted over its bare facade, and finished
occasions.note: The legend that Franz Joseph avoided the windows facing it is not recorded here.

occasions.label: Death of Mahler
Kokoschka paints Alma Mahler; their affair begins
Der Brenner's inquiry on Karl Kraus, with contributions by Schoenberg and Loos among others
occasions.note: The list of contributors and the issue (summer 1913) are to be checked.

occasions.label: The Skandalkonzert at the Musikverein: Webern, Zemlinsky, Schoenberg and Berg's Altenberg songs, broken off in a riot
occasions.note: Altenberg is present as the poet of the songs set; his attendance is not recorded.

occasions.label: Hitler leaves Vienna for Munich, evading Austrian military service
Einstein writes to Mach that his researches on the foundations of mechanics will be confirmed
occasions.note: 25 June 1913 is the date usually given.

occasions.label: Kokoschka paints The Bride of the Wind, himself and Alma
occasions.note: Painted chiefly in 1913 and finished early in 1914.

occasions.label: Hitler, traced by the Austrian authorities, mustered at Salzburg and found unfit for service
Alma Mahler ends her affair with Kokoschka
occasions.note: The break was drawn out through 1914; she married Gropius in August 1915.

occasions.label: Wittgenstein offers Ficker 100,000 crowns to distribute among Austrian artists in need
Ficker visits Wittgenstein in Vienna and takes him to meet Loos
occasions.note: Late July 1914.

occasions.label: Ficker distributes Wittgenstein's anonymous gift: Rilke and Trakl 20,000 crowns each, Kokoschka, Loos and others smaller sums
occasions.note: Decided at the end of July 1914; the dates of the distribution are approximate. The two large shares are firm; Loos's and Kokoschka's are to be checked.

occasions.label: Wittgenstein volunteers for the Austro-Hungarian army
Ficker visits Trakl in the garrison hospital at Kraków
Death of Trakl, of an overdose of cocaine, days before Wittgenstein reaches Kraków
occasions.note: Wittgenstein arrived on 6 November.

occasions.label: Kokoschka joins a regiment of dragoons
Rilke's letter of thanks for the gift, forwarded by Ficker to the anonymous donor
Kokoschka gravely wounded on the eastern front
Death of Mach
In Olmütz, Wittgenstein meets Paul Engelmann, Loos's pupil, to whom Loos had sent him
Death of Klimt; Schiele draws him on his deathbed
Death of Otto Wagner
Death of Schiele, of the influenza, three days after his wife
The armistice of Villa Giusti; Wittgenstein taken prisoner by the Italians
occasions.note: Wittgenstein's capture is dated 3 or 4 November.

occasions.label: Schoenberg founds the Society for Private Musical Performances, Berg and Webern among its directors of performance
Death of Altenberg; Kraus speaks at his grave, and Loos designs it
Back from captivity, Wittgenstein meets Loos and finds him changed
occasions.note: Wittgenstein to Engelmann, September 1919: Loos infected with the most virulent bogus intellectualism.

occasions.label: Die Frau ohne Schatten first performed at the State Opera, of which Strauss becomes co-director
Wittgenstein offers the Tractatus to Ficker for Der Brenner, its point being ethical; Ficker declines
The Logisch-philosophische Abhandlung in Ostwald's Annalen der Naturphilosophie; in English, with the German, in 1922
The Society's Johann Strauss evening: waltzes arranged by Schoenberg, Berg and Webern
occasions.note: 27 May 1921 is the day usually given; the arrangements were auctioned for the Society.

occasions.label: Schlick called to the chair of the philosophy of the inductive sciences, once Mach's and Boltzmann's
Kraus attacks Hofmannsthal's Salzburg Great Theatre of the World in Die Fackel
Freud writes to Schnitzler on his sixtieth birthday of having avoided him from a dread of meeting his double
Schnitzler dines with Freud at the Berggasse
occasions.note: Schnitzler's diary; 16 June 1922 is the day given.

occasions.label: Wozzeck in vocal score, dedicated to Alma Mahler, who helped pay for its printing
Schlick's Thursday evening circle begins to meet: the Vienna Circle
occasions.note: Hans Hahn, Herbert Feigl and others are not beings of this record.

occasions.label: Strauss leaves the State Opera after his quarrel with his co-director Schalk
Schlick writes to Wittgenstein of his own and his circle's admiration for the Tractatus, asking to meet
Carnap comes to Vienna as Privatdozent at Schlick's invitation, and joins the Circle
Gödel, a student, begins to attend the Circle
Margaret Stonborough commissions the house in the Kundmanngasse from Engelmann and her brother; built 1926-1928
occasions.note: Wittgenstein took the design over from Engelmann.

occasions.label: Freud meets Einstein in Berlin, at the house of his son Ernst
At Margaret Stonborough's, Wittgenstein meets Schlick
Wittgenstein meets members of the Circle, Schlick, Waismann, Carnap and Feigl, and reads them Tagore
occasions.note: Summer 1927, a series of meetings: an occasion of coarse resolution.

occasions.label: The manifesto Wissenschaftliche Weltauffassung: Der Wiener Kreis, dedicated to Schlick, naming Wittgenstein among its leading representatives
occasions.note: Written by Neurath, Carnap and Hahn; Wittgenstein disliked its self-satisfaction (to Waismann, 1929).

occasions.label: Death of Hofmannsthal, two days after his son's suicide
Wittgenstein's conversations at Schlick's house begin, recorded by Waismann (1929-1932)
In the Café Reichsrat, Gödel tells Carnap, Feigl and Waismann of his incompleteness result
occasions.note: From Carnap's diary.

occasions.label: At the conference on the epistemology of the exact sciences, Gödel announces his first incompleteness theorem; Waismann presents Wittgenstein's view
Zweig's Die Heilung durch den Geist, with its essay on Freud
Strauss, seeking a librettist after Hofmannsthal's death, meets Zweig
Wittgenstein writes to Schlick accusing Carnap of using his ideas without acknowledgement
Dollfuss becomes chancellor, Schuschnigg his minister of justice
Einstein and Freud exchange letters: Why War?
On holiday in the Tyrol, Carnap and Feigl read and discuss Popper's manuscript
Hitler's thousand-mark levy on travel to Austria; Dollfuss's government bans the Nazi party
Death of Loos; Kraus speaks at his grave
The February fighting: Dollfuss's government crushes the Social Democrats; Neurath, in Moscow, does not return
The Verein Ernst Mach, the Circle's public society, dissolved by the authorities
occasions.note: Schlick protested that the society was not political. The date is to be checked.

occasions.label: Dollfuss murdered in the Chancellery by Austrian Nazis in a failed putsch
occasions.note: What Hitler knew of the putsch beforehand is disputed.

occasions.label: Popper's Logik der Forschung, dated 1935, in the Circle's series edited by Schlick
occasions.note: Schlick accepted it for the series on condition that it be shortened.

occasions.label: Carnap reviews Logik der Forschung in Erkenntnis
Strauss's letter to Zweig, opened by the Gestapo; Strauss loses the presidency of the Reich Chamber of Music
The first International Congress for the Unity of Science; Popper among the speakers
Death of Berg
Death of Kraus
Schlick shot dead on the stairs of the University by a former student
occasions.note: The murderer, Johann Nelböck, was celebrated in part of the press and released after the Anschluss.

occasions.label: Hitler summons Schuschnigg to the Berghof and dictates terms
Schuschnigg resigns, German troops cross the border, and Austria is annexed
Freud leaves Vienna for exile in London
Zweig brings Dalí to Freud in London

ties.note: The last Fidelio follows his resignation under the press campaigns and intrigues of 1907; the sign is the break.
The crisis of summer 1910 (Gropius) falls between the attested meetings and is not signed.
Zemlinsky was Schoenberg's only teacher (from about 1895), and from 1901 his brother-in-law.
Schoenberg's harsh criticism of Berg in 1913-1915 is not coded.
Regard shown on both sides, with the rivalry of the two leading conductor-composers; both were at the Austrian premiere of Salome in Graz (16 May 1906), not an occasion here.
Their earlier operas (Elektra 1909, Der Rosenkavalier 1911) were first performed in Dresden and are not occasions of this record.
Die schweigsame Frau, on Zweig's libretto, was first performed in Dresden on 24 June 1935.
In 1935 Berg's Violin Concerto was written to the memory of Manon Gropius, Alma's daughter.
Coloured music by its theme, Beethoven and Mahler's performance in the Secession's homage. Klimt's word at the station, Vorbei, is from Paul Stefan's account.
In 1903 they founded the Wiener Werkstätte together (not an occasion here).
In 1905 Klimt withdrew from the commission and returned the fee.
Schiele sought Klimt out in 1907; Klimt encouraged and helped him.
The break was with his teacher Christian Griepenkerl.
A love affair; the codebook has no type for it, and friendship is the nearest.
Wittgenstein later named Loos among his influences (1931). The sign of 1919 rests on his letter to Engelmann.
Loos designed Altenberg's grave.
Coloured by its theme here, the house she commissioned. Klimt painted her portrait in 1905.
Kraus spoke at Altenberg's grave.
Kraus's war on the Presse and its editor Benedikt lasted his life; Die letzten Tage der Menschheit is one of its monuments.
Kraus spoke at Loos's grave.
The last sign is Ficker's refusal of the Tractatus, a refusal and not a quarrel: a mixed act, coded by what it is remembered for.
Ficker had published Trakl in Der Brenner since 1912.
Their correspondence ran from 1908.
Gödel attended until about 1928 and later distanced himself from the Circle's positivism.
Never a member; Neurath called him the Circle's official opposition. Regard was shown too: the book appeared in the Circle's own series.
Wittgenstein never attended the Circle's meetings; he met chosen members. The sign of 1929 is his displeasure at the manifesto.
Their joint book was abandoned in the mid-1930s; Wittgenstein's later coolness is not coded.
Wittgenstein stopped seeing Carnap early in 1929.
The tension between Schlick's and Neurath's wings of the Circle is not coded.
Gödel attended Schlick's seminar; the murder preceded one of his breakdowns.
A single analytic consultation; the codebook has no type for it, and collaboration is the nearest.
The sign of 1900 is his departure for Leipzig; he returned to his chair in 1902.
Einstein wrote Mach's obituary (1916). The preface to Mach's posthumous Optics (1921) rejecting relativity is of contested authenticity, and is not coded.
Coloured science by its theme: Freud recognises in Schnitzler's intuition the knowledge of his own research.
Neurath, a socialist and the Circle's political wing, against the government that crushed his party and dissolved his society.
